14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines total, with SKILL.md under 1000 lines and the rest in bundled resources (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. SKILL TEMPLATE (WITH BUNDLED RESOURCES)
116: 
117: **Use for**: Skills with bundled resources (references, scripts, or assets)
118: 
119: **Target**: 800-2000 lines (SKILL.md <1000 lines, rest in resources)

122: - Max 5000 words (3000 recommended)

126: 
127: Packaging enforcement note:
128: - `package_skill.py` fails if `REFERENCES` is missing and no approved combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES` structure exists.
129:

137: description: Example skill demonstrating proper template structure with specific capabilities for semantic code search and context preservation workflows.

449: ---
450: 
451: ## 4. SECTION-BY-SECTION CONTENT GUIDANCE
452: 
453: ### Section 1: WHEN TO USE
454: 
455: **Purpose**: Help the AI agent and users understand WHEN to activate this skill
456: 
457: **Section Boundary Rule**: "When to Use" = WHEN (triggers only). File references belong in Section 2 (Smart Routing).
458: 
459: **Essential Content** (ONLY these belong here):
460: - Activation triggers (what conditions activate this skill)
461: - Use case categories (2-4 categories)
462: - Specific scenarios (3-5 per category)
463: - Anti-patterns ("When NOT to Use")
464: - Keyword triggers (optional)
465: 
466: **Content that does NOT belong here** (move to Section 2 inline):
467: - ❌ File references
468: - ❌ Resource paths
469: - ❌ Resource tables
470: 
471: **Structure**:
472: 
473: ### Activation Triggers
474: 
475: **Use when**:
476: - [Specific scenario with context]
477: - [Specific scenario with context]
478: 
479: **Keyword Triggers**:
480: - [Pattern that activates skill]
481: 
482: ### Use Cases
483: 
484: ### [Use Case Category]
485: 
486: [Content for use case]
487: 
488: ### When NOT to Use
489: 
490: **Skip this skill when:**
491: - [Anti-pattern with rationale]
492: 
493: **Writing Tips**:
494: - Be specific: "Generate JSDoc for functions" not "document code"
495: - Include context: Why each scenario benefits from this skill
496: - Clear boundaries: Explicitly state what's out of scope
497: - Trigger patterns: What keywords/patterns auto-activate skill
498: - **NO file references** - those go in Section 2 (Smart Routing)
499: 
500: **Word Budget**: 100-200 lines
501: 
502: ---
503: 
504: ### Section 2: SMART ROUTING (Required for All Skills)
505: 
506: **Purpose**: Use this section to explain how you route a request to this skill's resources.
507: 
508: **Three skill kinds, one shape**:
509: 
510: | Kind | How to tell | What Section 2 says |
511: |------|-------------|---------------------|
512: | Hub | the folder holds `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` | how a prompt reaches a mode, and where the root `ROUTER.md` is |
513: | Mode packet | a packet folder inside a hub | what selects this packet, what it loads first, and where its own `ROUTER.md` is |
514: | Standalone | neither hub file | the same as a mode packet, with the router in its own `ROUTER.md` |
515: 
516: **The limit**: 12 non-blank lines and 180 words are the hard ceilings the check enforces. Aim for 8 to 12 lines. A packet or standalone skill says three things: what selects it, what it loads first, and where the machine router is.
517: 
518: **The sibling router**: the machine router lives in `ROUTER.md` beside `SKILL.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading.
519: That heading is the one every reader parses. Its section number is optional, so `## MACHINE ROUTER` and `## 9. MACHINE ROUTER` both count, and the check ignores the number.
520: Keep pseudocode out of SMART ROUTING and put it in that section.
521: `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own: two homes for one router is the dual declaration the check reports.
522: 
523: **The link line**: Section 2 names the router file with a relative markdown link, [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md), and its target resolves on disk. A sentence that mentions the name without a link fails, because a reader cannot follow it to a file that is not there.
524: 
525: **One router per folder**: every skill and every mode packet owns `ROUTER.md` inside its own folder, linked from its own `SKILL.md`. A router file whose real path leaves the folder is not that skill's router.
526: 
527: **The no-match outcome** is named `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` everywhere. Low confidence returns a disambiguation checklist, never an empty result and never a guess.
528: 
529: **Validation**: `package_skill.py --strict` reports the routing shape with five codes:
530: 
531: | Code | Finding |
532: |------|---------|
533: | `RS-001` | SMART ROUTING is longer than the limit (12 lines or 180 words by default) |
534: | `RS-002` | `SKILL.md` carries a `## MACHINE ROUTER` section, with or without a code block |
535: | `RS-003` | A `## MACHINE ROUTER` section is not the last H2 of the document that holds it |
536: | `RS-004` | the skill has no sibling `ROUTER.md`, or its real path leaves the skill folder |
537: | `RS-005` | `SKILL.md` has no relative markdown link to `./ROUTER.md` that resolves |
538: 
539: The machine block itself is a fenced block or an unfenced run of indented lines.
540: It declares the router with one of these markers: `INTENT_SIGNALS =`, `RESOURCE_MAP =`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE =`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST =`, `def discover_markdown_resources` or `def _guard_in_skill`.
541: A fence closes only on a run of the same character that is at least as long as its opening run.
542: 
543: **Known debt** is listed in `sk-create-skill/scripts/routing-shape-known-debt.json`.
544: Entries use skill paths relative to `.skilled/skills`, such as `sk-code/sk-code-review`.
545: A folder outside that root is never debt.
546: Each entry records `{"lines", "words", "machineBlocks", "codes"}`.
547: A listed skill fails if its line count, word count or machine blocks left in `SKILL.md` exceed the record, or if it adds an unrecorded code.
548: The checker ignores entries in any other form.
549: Remove an entry when the skill follows the canon.
550: 
551: **Placement**: the SMART ROUTING section sits after Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) and before HOW IT WORKS, and `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md` at the skill root.
552: 
553: **Worked example** (a canon Section 2 and its sibling router, nothing else):
554: 
555: \## 2. SMART ROUTING
556: 
557: Use this skill for [domain] work: [trigger 1], [trigger 2], or [trigger 3].
558: The first signal is [project/stack/mode detection], because it picks the knowledge folder before any intent scoring.
559: Load `references/[default].md` first on every run. The other files assume it.
560: Then load what the matched intent maps to: [intent A] reads `references/[domain]/[a].md`, and [intent B] reads `assets/[domain]/[b].md`.
561: Keep every path inside this skill folder and load a file only when it exists.
562: When two intents score close together, follow both in rank order.
563: When nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist from the machine router instead of guessing.
564: The machine router lives in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md); read it before selecting a resource.
565: 
566: ---
567: 
568: The link resolves to the sibling file, whose one heading the readers parse is:
569: 
570: \## MACHINE ROUTER
571: 
572: ```python
573: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/[default].md"
574: INTENT_SIGNALS = {"PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": [("[keyword]", 4), ("[phrase]", 3)]}}
575: RESOURCE_MAP = {"PRIMARY": ["references/[domain]/[primary].md"]}
576: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = ["Confirm the routing key", "Confirm the intent", "Provide one concrete input"]
577: 
578: def route_[skill_name]_resources(user_request, task=None):
579:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
580:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)
581:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 0.5:
582:         return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}
583:     return {"routing_key": get_routing_key(task, [primary]), "resources": inventory}
584: ```
585: 
586: The full resilience pattern (guarded paths, recursive discovery, routing keys) is in [skill-smart-router.md](./skill-smart-router.md).
587: 
588: **Writing Tips**:
589: - Open Section 2 with the signal that actually picks this skill's files.
590: - Name the first file to load, so a reader knows where to start.
591: - Name the router file with a markdown link, so a reader can open it.
592: - Keep `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` as the named no-match outcome.
593: - Edit `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` in `ROUTER.md` when the skill gains a domain.
594: - Avoid duplicate lookup tables, static file inventories, and unguarded `load()` calls.
595: 
596: **Word Budget**: 8-12 non-blank lines of prose
597: 
598: ---
599: 
600: ### Section 3: HOW IT WORKS
601: 
602: **Purpose**: Explain the skill's workflow, architecture, and key patterns
603: 
604: **Essential Content**:
605: - Process flow (visual diagram using ASCII)
606: - Key capabilities or components
607: - Configuration or setup requirements
608: - Examples of primary workflows
609: - Flowchart supplements for complex logic (NEW - when logic blocks present)
610: 
611: **Structure**:
612: 
613: ### [Primary Workflow Name]
614: 
615: [Brief explanation]
616: 
617: **Process Flow**:
618: \`\`\`
619: STEP 1: [Action]
620:    ├─ [Sub-task]
621:    └─ [Output]
622:    ↓
623: STEP 2: [Action]
624:    └─ [Output]
625: \`\`\`
626: 
627: **Example**:
628: \`\`\`[language]
629: # Realistic example
630: \`\`\`
631: 
632: **Writing Tips**:
633: - Use Mermaid for flow diagrams so a parser can read them.
634: - Show, don't just tell (include code examples)
635: - Progressive detail: Overview → specifics → edge cases
636: - Link to references for deep dives
637: - **Flowchart Supplements**: Add visual flowcharts before/after complex Python/YAML logic (see below)
638: 
639: **Word Budget**: 150-300 lines
640: 
641: ### Flowchart Supplements (For Complex Logic)
642: 
643: **Purpose**: Add visual clarity to complex Python/YAML logic blocks without removing structured code
644: 
645: **When to Use**:
646: - Complex conditional logic (nested if/else, multiple branches)
647: - Mode detection algorithms
648: - Multi-step decision trees
649: - Workflow routing logic
650: - State machine transitions
651: 
652: **Approach**:
653: - **Supplement, don't replace**: Keep existing Python/YAML code intact
654: - **Add flowcharts**: Place ASCII flowchart before or after code block
655: - **Visual aid purpose**: Help quick understanding of logic flow
656: 
657: **Structure**:
658: 
659: ### [Logic Section Name]
660: 
661: **[Brief explanation of what this logic does]**
662: 
663: **Logic Flow**:
664: \`\`\`
665: START
666:   ↓
667: [Check Condition A]
668:   ↓
669: A True? ─── NO ──→ [Path B]
670:   │                    ↓
671:   │              [Process B]
672:   │                    ↓
673:   YES              [Continue]
674:   ↓
675: [Process A]
676:   ↓
677: RESULT
678: \`\`\`
679: 
680: **Implementation**:
681: \`\`\`python
682: def example_logic(input):
683:     """Original Python logic preserved"""
684:     if condition_a:
685:         return process_a(input)
686:     else:
687:         return process_b(input)
688: \`\`\`
689: 
690: **OR for configuration:**
691: 
692: \`\`\`yaml
693: mode_detection:
694:   trigger_patterns:
695:     ticket: ["$ticket", "create ticket"]
696:     story: ["$story", "user story"]
697:   defaults:
698:     mode: interactive
699:     depth: 10
700: \`\`\`
701: 
702: **Writing Tips**:
703: - **Keep code**: Don't remove Python/YAML - it's precise and complete
704: - **Add diagrams**: Flowcharts provide at-a-glance understanding
705: - **Placement**:
706:   - Flowchart FIRST if it aids comprehension before reading code
707:   - Flowchart AFTER if it summarizes complex code
708:   - Both before AND after for very complex logic
709: - **Consistency**: Use the same ASCII flowchart style as the other diagrams in the file
710: - **When to skip**: Simple 2-3 line logic doesn't need flowcharts
711: 
712: **Example Use Cases**:
713: - Mode detection with 5+ conditions → Flowchart + Python code
714: - YAML configuration with complex triggers → Keep YAML, add decision tree diagram
715: - Multi-step workflow routing → Flowchart showing paths, keep implementation code
716: 
717: **Word Budget**: Variable (adds 10-30 lines per complex logic block)
718: 
719: ---
720: 
721: ### Section 4: RULES (REQUIRED)
722: 
723: **Purpose**: Define mandatory behaviors, prohibited actions, and escalation triggers
724: 
725: **Validation**: package_skill.py requires this section with specific subsections
726: 
727: **Essential Content** (all three subsections REQUIRED):
728: - ALWAYS rules (4-7 critical requirements)
729: - NEVER rules (3-5 anti-patterns to avoid)
730: - ESCALATE IF (3-5 situations requiring user input)
731: 
732: **Structure**:
733: 
734: ### ALWAYS
735: 
736: **ALWAYS do these without asking:**
737: 
738: 1. **ALWAYS [requirement]**
739:    - [Why this matters]
740:    - [Implementation detail]
741: 
742: ### NEVER
743: 
744: **NEVER do these:**
745: 
746: 1. **NEVER [anti-pattern]**
747:    - [Why problematic]
748:    - [Alternative approach]
749: 
750: ### ESCALATE IF
751: 
752: **Ask user when:**
753: 
754: 1. **ESCALATE IF [ambiguous situation]**
755:    - [What's unclear]
756:    - [What clarification needed]
757: 
758: **Writing Tips**:
759: - Use ALL CAPS for subsection headers: `ALWAYS`, `NEVER`, `ESCALATE IF` (or `ESCALATE WHEN`)
760: - Be specific and actionable
761: - Explain *why* for each rule (rationale matters)
762: - Include implementation guidance
763: - Present options to user for ESCALATE IF cases
764: 
765: **Word Budget**: 100-200 lines
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ### Section 5: REFERENCES
770: 
771: **Purpose**: Expose the operational references and templates the skill depends on.
772: 
773: **Essential Content**:
774: - Core references used during execution
775: - Templates/assets used during output generation
776: - Loading notes that stay consistent with Section 2 (SMART ROUTING)
777: 
778: **Structure**:
779: 
780: ### Core References
781: - [reference-name.md](./references/reference-name.md) - Primary guidance
782: 
783: ### Templates and Assets
784: - [template-name.md](./assets/template-name.md) - Reusable output template
785: 
786: ### Reference Loading Notes
787: - Load only what current intent requires.
788: - Keep Smart Routing as the single routing authority.
789: 
790: **Word Budget**: 40-120 lines
791: 
792: ---
793: 
794: ### Section 6: SUCCESS CRITERIA
795: 
796: **Purpose**: Define completion conditions and quality standards
797: 
798: **Essential Content**:
799: - Completion checklist (5-10 items)
800: - Quality gates or thresholds
801: - Validation requirements
802: 
803: **Structure**:
804: 
805: ### Task Completion Checklist
806: 
807: **[Workflow name] Complete When:**
808: 
809: - [ ] [Success criterion 1]
810: - [ ] [Success criterion 2]
811: - [ ] [Success criterion 3]
812: 
813: ### Quality Gates
814: 
815: **Before marking complete:**
816: 
817: - **[Dimension]**: [Specific requirement]
818: - **[Dimension]**: [Specific requirement]
819: 
820: **Writing Tips**:
821: - Use checkbox format `- [ ]` for checklists
822: - Specific and measurable criteria
823: - Include both completion and quality checks
824: - Define thresholds numerically where possible
825: 
826: **Word Budget**: 50-120 lines
827: 
828: ---
829: 
830: ### Section 7: INTEGRATION POINTS
831: 
832: **Purpose**: Document how skill integrates with systems, tools, and workflow contracts
833: 
834: **Essential Content**:
835: - Validation workflow integration
836: - Required workflow contracts and handoff rules
837: - Tool usage patterns
838: - Knowledge base dependencies
839: - External tool requirements
840: 
841: **Structure**:
842: 
843: ### Validation Workflow Integration
844: 
845: **[Validation Name]**:
846: - Triggers: [When to run]
847: - Purpose: [What it validates]
848: 
849: ### Cross-Workflow Contracts
850: 
851: **[Contract Name]**: [When it applies and what the skill must hand off]
852: 
853: ### Tool Usage Guidelines
854: 
855: **[Tool]**: [Usage pattern]
856: 
857: ### Knowledge Base Dependencies
858: 
859: - **Required**: [Files needed]
860: - **Optional**: [Enhancing files]
861: 
862: ### External Tools
863: 
864: **[Tool Name]**:
865: - Installation: [How]
866: - Purpose: [Why]
867: 
868: **Writing Tips**:
869: - Distinguish required vs. optional dependencies
870: - Provide installation/setup instructions for external tools
871: - Explain fallback behavior if optional resources missing
872: - Link related skills by name
873: 
874: **Word Budget**: 50-150 lines
875: 
876: ---
877: 
878: ## 5. COMMON PITFALLS
879: 
880: For the complete list of 8 common pitfalls with before/after examples, see:
881: → **[common-pitfalls.md](../../references/shared/common-pitfalls.md)**
882: 
883: **Quick Summary:**
884: 1. Generic descriptions → Be specific about capabilities
885: 2. Bloated SKILL.md → Move details to references/
886: 3. Missing bundled resources → Identify repeated code/docs
887: 4. Unclear triggers → Specific activation conditions
888: 5. Distant instructions → Use the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist)
889: 6. Platform-specific claims → Stay platform-agnostic
890: 7. Multiline YAML descriptions → Keep single line
891: 8. Redundant routing tables → Keep routing authority in pseudocode
892: 
893: ### Writing Style Quick Reference
894: 
895: For instructions and README prose, use the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist).

898: 
899: ## 6. QUALITY CHECKLIST & QUICK REFERENCE
900: 
901: ### Pre-Packaging Checklist
902: 
903: **Before running package_skill.py:**
904: 
905: Frontmatter:
906: □ YAML frontmatter present and valid
907: □ Required fields: name, description, allowed-tools
908: □ Name is hyphen-case (matches directory)
909: □ Description uses third-person voice
910: □ Description is specific (not generic)
911: □ No angle brackets in description
912: □ allowed-tools lists all tools used
913: 
914: Structure:
915: □ H1 title with descriptive subtitle
916: □ Numbered H2 sections for the body (1. WHEN TO USE, 2. SMART ROUTING, etc.)
917: □ H2 headings use ALL CAPS
918: □ Section separators (---) between major sections
919: □ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
920: □ Proper heading hierarchy (H1 → H2 → H3)
921: □ SMART ROUTING section placed after WHEN TO USE, before HOW IT WORKS
922: 
923: Content - Standard Sections:
924: □ WHEN TO USE section includes use cases + anti-patterns
925: □ HOW IT WORKS section explains workflow clearly
926: □ RULES section has ALWAYS, NEVER, ESCALATE IF
927: □ REFERENCES section lists core references/templates explicitly
928: □ SUCCESS CRITERIA section defines completion
929: □ INTEGRATION POINTS section documents dependencies
930: □ All bundled resources referenced from SKILL.md
931: □ No duplication between SKILL.md and references/
932: 
933: Content - Routing Canon:
934: □ Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) contains ONLY activation triggers and use cases
935: □ Section 1 does NOT contain file-path routing logic
936: □ SMART ROUTING section exists (Section 2 - REQUIRED for all skills)
937: □ Section 2 is 8-12 non-blank lines of plain prose: what selects this skill, what it loads first, where the machine router is
938: □ Section 2 names the no-match outcome `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK`
939: □ Any machine router block sits in the sibling `ROUTER.md`, never inside SMART ROUTING
940: □ `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own
941: □ Section 2 links to [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) with a relative markdown link that resolves
942: □ `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md`, and every path in it stays inside the skill folder
943: □ Flowchart supplements added to complex logic blocks in Section 3 (where applicable)
944: □ Python/YAML code preserved (supplements, not replacements)
945: □ Mermaid diagrams use valid syntax (when used)
946: 
947: Quality:
948: □ SKILL.md under 5k words (<3k preferred)
949: □ Concrete examples included
950: □ Rationale provided for rules
951: □ Instructions follow the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist)
952: □ Consistent heading format
953: □ All code blocks specify language
954: □ Links work correctly
955: □ Section 1 contains ONLY triggers/use cases (NO file references)
956: □ `MACHINE ROUTER` pseudocode guards every path and checks that the file exists
957: 
958: ### Quick Reference Table
959: 
960: | Element               | Requirement                | Example                                                                                            |
961: | --------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
962: | **Filename**          | `SKILL.md` (exact case)    | ✅ `SKILL.md`  ❌ `skill.md`                                                                         |
963: | **Frontmatter**       | Required YAML with fields  | `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`                                                             |
964: | **Name Format**       | `hyphen-case`              | ✅ `mcp-chrome-devtools`  ❌ `devtools_cli`                                                    |
965: | **Description Voice** | Third-person               | ✅ "Use when..."  ❌ "You should..."                                                                 |

968: | **Sections**          | 5 required + 3 recommended | Required: WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES (or combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES`). Recommended: SUCCESS CRITERIA, INTEGRATION POINTS, REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES |

971: | **Rules Format**      | ALWAYS, NEVER, ESCALATE IF | All caps headers, specific rules                                                                   |
972: | **Examples**          | Concrete and realistic     | Show actual use cases                                                                              |
973: 
974: ### Template Selection Matrix
975: 
976: | Characteristic        | Simple                    | Moderate                         | Complex                             |
977: | --------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
978: | **Workflows**         | Single                    | Single                           | Multiple modes                      |
979: | **Bundled Resources** | None                      | Some (refs/scripts/assets)       | Extensive                           |
980: | **Total Lines**       | 400-800                   | 800-2000                         | 2000-5000                           |
981: | **SKILL.md Lines**    | 400-800                   | 800-1000                         | <3000                               |
982: | **Sections**          | 5 required core           | 5 required + recommended sections | 5 required per mode + overview       |

18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines total, with SKILL.md under 1000 lines and the rest in bundled resources (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73:

76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)

400: \## 8. REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES
401: 
402: The router in `ROUTER.md` discovers reference, asset, and script docs dynamically. Start with `references/[primary].md`, `assets/[template].md`, and any skill-specific automation under `scripts/`, then load task-specific resources according to Section 2.
403: 
404: Scripts: `scripts/[primary-helper]` when the skill ships automation. Omit this line when no scripts exist.
405: 
406: Related skills: `[related-skill]` for [relationship], `[other-skill]` for [relationship], and `system-spec-kit` when packet documentation or memory continuity applies.
407: 
408: Install guide: [INSTALL-GUIDE.md](INSTALL-GUIDE.md) when the skill has installation or configuration steps.
409:

411: 
412: **Word Count Targets**:
413: - Section 1 (WHEN TO USE): 150-200 lines
414: - Section 2 (SMART ROUTING): 8-12 non-blank lines of plain prose (the router block lives in the sibling `ROUTER.md`)
415: - Section 3 (HOW IT WORKS): 200-300 lines
416: - Section 4 (RULES): 150-200 lines
417: - Section 5 (REFERENCES): 40-120 lines
418: - Section 6 (SUCCESS CRITERIA): 80-120 lines
419: - Section 7 (INTEGRATION POINTS): 100-150 lines
420: - Section 8 (REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES): 20-60 lines
421: 
422: **Bundled Resources Structure (Monolithic)**:
423: ```
424: .skilled/skills/skill-name/       # Note: .skilled/skills/ (singular, NOT skills)
425: ├── SKILL.md (800-1000 lines)
426: └── Bundled Resources
427:     ├── scripts/          - Executable automation
428:     ├── references/       - Detailed documentation (flat or domain subfolders)
429:     └── assets/           - Templates and examples (subfolders OK)
430:         ├── opencode/     - OpenCode component templates (skills, agents, commands)
431:         └── readme/        - README-shaped scaffolds (README, install guide)
432: ```
433: 
434: **Folder Organization Principle**:
435: - **references/** = flat for small skills, domain subfolders for medium/complex skills
436:   - Flat example: `references/core-standards.md`, `references/validation.md`
437:   - Domain example: `references/backend/go/`, `references/frontend/react/`
438: - **assets/** = Subfolders ALLOWED when organizing many files by category
439:   - Group related templates together
440:   - Example: `assets/skill/`, `assets/readme/`, `assets/flowcharts/`
441: - **scripts/** = Typically flat, but subfolders OK for large script collections
442: 
443: **Native Discovery**:
444: - Skills auto-discovered from `.skilled/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter
445: - Skill name in frontmatter MUST match folder name
446: - Skills appear as `skills_<name>` functions in OpenCode (hyphens → underscores)
447: - Invoke via `Read(".skilled/skills/<name>/SKILL.md")`

453: ### Section 1: WHEN TO USE
454: 
455: **Purpose**: Help the AI agent and users understand WHEN to activate this skill

462: - Specific scenarios (3-5 per category)
463: - Anti-patterns ("When NOT to Use")
464: - Keyword triggers (optional)
465: 
466: **Content that does NOT belong here** (move to Section 2 inline):
467: - ❌ File references
468: - ❌ Resource paths
469: - ❌ Resource tables
470: 
471: **Structure**:
472: 
473: ### Activation Triggers
474: 
475: **Use when**:
476: - [Specific scenario with context]
477: - [Specific scenario with context]
478: 
479: **Keyword Triggers**:
480: - [Pattern that activates skill]
481: 
482: ### Use Cases
483:

485: 
486: [Content for use case]
487: 
488: ### When NOT to Use
489: 
490: **Skip this skill when:**
491: - [Anti-pattern with rationale]
492: 
493: **Writing Tips**:
494: - Be specific: "Generate JSDoc for functions" not "document code"
495: - Include context: Why each scenario benefits from this skill
496: - Clear boundaries: Explicitly state what's out of scope
497: - Trigger patterns: What keywords/patterns auto-activate skill
498: - **NO file references** - those go in Section 2 (Smart Routing)
499:

503: 
504: ### Section 2: SMART ROUTING (Required for All Skills)
505: 
506: **Purpose**: Use this section to explain how you route a request to this skill's resources.
507: 
508: **Three skill kinds, one shape**:
509: 
510: | Kind | How to tell | What Section 2 says |
511: |------|-------------|---------------------|
512: | Hub | the folder holds `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` | how a prompt reaches a mode, and where the root `ROUTER.md` is |
513: | Mode packet | a packet folder inside a hub | what selects this packet, what it loads first, and where its own `ROUTER.md` is |
514: | Standalone | neither hub file | the same as a mode packet, with the router in its own `ROUTER.md` |
515: 
516: **The limit**: 12 non-blank lines and 180 words are the hard ceilings the check enforces. Aim for 8 to 12 lines. A packet or standalone skill says three things: what selects it, what it loads first, and where the machine router is.
517: 
518: **The sibling router**: the machine router lives in `ROUTER.md` beside `SKILL.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading.
519: That heading is the one every reader parses. Its section number is optional, so `## MACHINE ROUTER` and `## 9. MACHINE ROUTER` both count, and the check ignores the number.
520: Keep pseudocode out of SMART ROUTING and put it in that section.
521: `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own: two homes for one router is the dual declaration the check reports.
522: 
523: **The link line**: Section 2 names the router file with a relative markdown link, [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md), and its target resolves on disk. A sentence that mentions the name without a link fails, because a reader cannot follow it to a file that is not there.
524: 
525: **One router per folder**: every skill and every mode packet owns `ROUTER.md` inside its own folder, linked from its own `SKILL.md`. A router file whose real path leaves the folder is not that skill's router.
526: 
527: **The no-match outcome** is named `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` everywhere. Low confidence returns a disambiguation checklist, never an empty result and never a guess.
528: 
529: **Validation**: `package_skill.py --strict` reports the routing shape with five codes:
530: 
531: | Code | Finding |
532: |------|---------|
533: | `RS-001` | SMART ROUTING is longer than the limit (12 lines or 180 words by default) |
534: | `RS-002` | `SKILL.md` carries a `## MACHINE ROUTER` section, with or without a code block |
535: | `RS-003` | A `## MACHINE ROUTER` section is not the last H2 of the document that holds it |
536: | `RS-004` | the skill has no sibling `ROUTER.md`, or its real path leaves the skill folder |
537: | `RS-005` | `SKILL.md` has no relative markdown link to `./ROUTER.md` that resolves |
538: 
539: The machine block itself is a fenced block or an unfenced run of indented lines.
540: It declares the router with one of these markers: `INTENT_SIGNALS =`, `RESOURCE_MAP =`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE =`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST =`, `def discover_markdown_resources` or `def _guard_in_skill`.
541: A fence closes only on a run of the same character that is at least as long as its opening run.
542: 
543: **Known debt** is listed in `sk-create-skill/scripts/routing-shape-known-debt.json`.
544: Entries use skill paths relative to `.skilled/skills`, such as `sk-code/sk-code-review`.
545: A folder outside that root is never debt.
546: Each entry records `{"lines", "words", "machineBlocks", "codes"}`.
547: A listed skill fails if its line count, word count or machine blocks left in `SKILL.md` exceed the record, or if it adds an unrecorded code.
548: The checker ignores entries in any other form.
549: Remove an entry when the skill follows the canon.
550: 
551: **Placement**: the SMART ROUTING section sits after Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) and before HOW IT WORKS, and `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md` at the skill root.
552: 
553: **Worked example** (a canon Section 2 and its sibling router, nothing else):
554: 
555: \## 2. SMART ROUTING
556: 
557: Use this skill for [domain] work: [trigger 1], [trigger 2], or [trigger 3].
558: The first signal is [project/stack/mode detection], because it picks the knowledge folder before any intent scoring.
559: Load `references/[default].md` first on every run. The other files assume it.
560: Then load what the matched intent maps to: [intent A] reads `references/[domain]/[a].md`, and [intent B] reads `assets/[domain]/[b].md`.
561: Keep every path inside this skill folder and load a file only when it exists.
562: When two intents score close together, follow both in rank order.
563: When nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist from the machine router instead of guessing.
564: The machine router lives in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md); read it before selecting a resource.
565: 
566: ---
567: 
568: The link resolves to the sibling file, whose one heading the readers parse is:
569: 
570: \## MACHINE ROUTER
571: 
572: ```python
573: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/[default].md"
574: INTENT_SIGNALS = {"PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": [("[keyword]", 4), ("[phrase]", 3)]}}
575: RESOURCE_MAP = {"PRIMARY": ["references/[domain]/[primary].md"]}
576: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = ["Confirm the routing key", "Confirm the intent", "Provide one concrete input"]
577: 
578: def route_[skill_name]_resources(user_request, task=None):
579:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
580:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)
581:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 0.5:
582:         return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}
583:     return {"routing_key": get_routing_key(task, [primary]), "resources": inventory}
584: ```
585: 
586: The full resilience pattern (guarded paths, recursive discovery, routing keys) is in [skill-smart-router.md](./skill-smart-router.md).
587: 
588: **Writing Tips**:
589: - Open Section 2 with the signal that actually picks this skill's files.
590: - Name the first file to load, so a reader knows where to start.
591: - Name the router file with a markdown link, so a reader can open it.
592: - Keep `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` as the named no-match outcome.
593: - Edit `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` in `ROUTER.md` when the skill gains a domain.
594: - Avoid duplicate lookup tables, static file inventories, and unguarded `load()` calls.
595: 
596: **Word Budget**: 8-12 non-blank lines of prose
597:

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills

16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.

18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
23: 
24: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
25: 
26: **Core Purpose**:
27: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
28: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
29: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
30: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
31: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
32: 
33: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
34: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
35: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
36: 
37: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
38: 
39: ```
40: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
41:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
42:             ↓
43: Level 2: SKILL.md body
44:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
45:             ↓
46: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
47:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
48: ```
49: 
50: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
51: 
52: ### Location & Naming
53: 
54: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
55: 
56: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
57: 
58: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
59: |---------------|-----------------|
60: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
61: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
62: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
63: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
64: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |

68: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
69: 
70: ### Title and Intro
71: 
72: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
73: 
74: ```markdown
75: ---
76: title: [Title]
77: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
78: trigger_phrases:
79:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
80:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
81:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
82: importance_tier: normal
83: contextType: general
84: version: 1.0.0.0
85: ---
86: 
87: # [Title]
88: 
89: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: \## 1. OVERVIEW
94: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
95: 
96: ```
97: 
98: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block. The Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal:
99: - 3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content
100: - `importance_tier`, which defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs
101: - `contextType`, one of `planning|research|implementation|general`
102: 
103: See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
104: 
105: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
106: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
107: 
108: #### GOOD Intro Structure
109: 
110: ```markdown
111: # Git Commit Workflows
112: 
113: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: \## 1. OVERVIEW
118: 
119: ### Purpose
120: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
121: 
122: ### When to Use
123: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
124: - Filtering generated files from commits
125: - Writing clear commit messages
126: 
127: ### Core Principle
128: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
129: ```
130: 
131: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
132: 
133: ```markdown
134: # Git Commit Workflows
135: 
136: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
137: 
138: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
139: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
140: 
141: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
142: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: \## 1. OVERVIEW
147: 
148: ### Purpose
149: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
150: 
151: ### Core Principle
152: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
153: ```

156: 
157: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
158: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
159: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
160: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
161: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
162: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
163: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
164: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
165: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |

170: 
171: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.

175: 
176: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 1. OVERVIEW
181: 
182: ### Purpose
183: 
184: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
185: 
186: ### When to Use

188: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
189: - [Second trigger]
190: 
191: ### Core Principle
192: 
193: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
194: 
195: ### Boundaries
196: 
197: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]

199: 
200: ### Key Sources

211: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]

228: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

685: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
686: 
687: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
688: 
689: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
690: 
691: **Decision Criteria**:
692: 
693: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
694: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
695: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
696: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
697: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
698: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
699: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
700: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
701: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
702: 
703: ### Extraction Pattern
704: 
705: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
706: ```markdown
707: ### [Workflow Name]
708: 
709: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
710: 
711: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
712: 
713: **Quick Overview**:
714: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
715: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
716: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
717: 
718: **Configuration Options:**
719: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
720: - Default values optimized for common use cases
721: ```
722: 
723: ### Benefits of Separation
724: 
725: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
726: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
727: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
728: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
729: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
730: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
731: 
732: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
733: 
734: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
735: \```python
736: def detect_mode(request):
737:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
738:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
739:     return 'interactive', 10
740: \```
741: 
742: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
743: 
744: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
745: \```python
746: from dataclasses import dataclass
747: 
748: @dataclass
749: class ModeConfig:
750:     mode: str
751:     depth_rounds: int
752: 
753: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
754:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
755:     if '$quick' in request:
756:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
757:     elif '$ticket' in request:
758:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
759:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
760: \```
761: 
762: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
763: \```python
764: def test_quick_mode():
765:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
766: \```
767: 
768: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
769:

772: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
773: 
774: ### Purpose
775: 
776: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
777: 
778: **When to use YAML**:
779: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
780: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
781: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
782: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
783: - Validation schemas
784: 
785: ### Standard YAML Structure
786: 
787: ```yaml
788: # [config-name].yaml
789: metadata:
790:   version: "1.0.0"
791:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
792: 
793: config:
794:   threshold_values:
795:     low: 1
796:     medium: 5
797:     high: 10
798:   feature_flags:
799:     enable_feature_x: true
800:   mappings:
801:     $quick: "quick_mode"
802:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
803: ```
804: 
805: ### File Organization
806: 
807: ```
808: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
809: ├── assets/
810: │   ├── workflow-configs/
811: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
812: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
813: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
814: │   ├── mappings/
815: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
816: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
817: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
818: │   └── templates/
819: │       └── [template files]
820: ```
821: 
822: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
823: 
824: ```python
825: import yaml
826: from pathlib import Path
827: 
828: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
829:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
830:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
831:     with open(config_path) as f:
832:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
833: 
834: # Usage
835: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
836: ```
837: 
838: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
839: 
840: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
841: ```markdown
842: | Trigger                    | Action             |
843: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
844: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
845: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
846: ```
847: 
848: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
849: 
850: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
851: ```yaml
852: config:
853:   variant_triggers:
854:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
855:     implicit:
856:       complexity_threshold: 7
857:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
858:   variant_count:
859:     simple: [2, 3]
860:     complex: [5, 10]
861: ```
862: 
863: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
864: ```python
865: import yaml
866: 
867: class VariantDetector:
868:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
869:         with open(config_path) as f:
870:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
871: 
872:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
873:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
874:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
875:             return True
876: 
877:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
878:         if complexity >= threshold:
879:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
880:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
881:         return False
882: ```
883: 
884: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
885:

888: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
889: 
890: ### When to Use Python for Logic
891: 
892: **Use Python scripts when**:
893: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
894: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
895: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
896: - API integration (external services)
897: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
898: 
899: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
900: 
901: **Always include**:
902: - Type hints for parameters and return values
903: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
904: - Dataclasses for structured data
905: 
906: **Example**:
907: ```python
908: from dataclasses import dataclass
909: from pathlib import Path
910: 
911: @dataclass
912: class ValidationResult:
913:     is_valid: bool
914:     errors: list[str]
915: 
916: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
917:     """
918:     Validate configuration file.
919: 
920:     Args:
921:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
922: 
923:     Returns:
924:         ValidationResult with status and errors
925: 
926:     Raises:
927:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
928:     """
929:     if not config_path.exists():
930:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
931:     # Validation logic
932:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
933: ```
934: 
935: ### Unit Testing Requirements
936: 
937: **Every Python script must have tests**:
938: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
939: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
940: - Framework: pytest
941: 
942: **Example**:
943: ```python
944: import pytest
945: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
946: 
947: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
948:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
949:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
950:     result = validate_config(config)
951:     assert result.is_valid
952: 
953: def test_validate_missing_file():
954:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
955:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
956: ```
957: 
958: ### Import and Reference Patterns
959: 
960: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
961: 
962: **Markdown references**:
963: ```markdown
964: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
965: ```
966: 
967: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
968: 
969: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
970: ```markdown
971: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
972: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
973: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
974: ```
975: 
976: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
977: 
978: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
979: ```python
980: from typing import Literal
981: from dataclasses import dataclass
982: 
983: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
984: 
985: @dataclass
986: class WorkflowDecision:
987:     mode: WorkflowMode
988:     depth_rounds: int
989: 
990: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
991:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
992:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
993:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
994:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
995:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
996:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
997: ```
998: 
999: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
1000: ```python
1001: def test_quick_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1003: 
1004: def test_default_mode():
1005:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1006: ```
1007: 
1008: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
23: 
24: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
25: 
26: **Core Purpose**:
27: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
28: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
29: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
30: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
31: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
32: 
33: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
34: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
35: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
36: 
37: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
38: 
39: ```
40: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
41:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
42:             ↓
43: Level 2: SKILL.md body
44:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
45:             ↓
46: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
47:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
48: ```
49: 
50: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
51: 
52: ### Location & Naming
53: 
54: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
55: 
56: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
57: 
58: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
59: |---------------|-----------------|
60: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
61: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
62: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
63: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
64: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
65: 
66: ---
67: 
68: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
69: 
70: ### Title and Intro
71: 
72: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
73: 
74: ```markdown
75: ---
76: title: [Title]
77: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
78: trigger_phrases:
79:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
80:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
81:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
82: importance_tier: normal
83: contextType: general
84: version: 1.0.0.0
85: ---
86: 
87: # [Title]
88: 
89: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: \## 1. OVERVIEW
94: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
95: 
96: ```
97: 
98: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block. The Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal:
99: - 3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content
100: - `importance_tier`, which defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs
101: - `contextType`, one of `planning|research|implementation|general`
102: 
103: See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
104: 
105: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
106: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
107: 
108: #### GOOD Intro Structure
109: 
110: ```markdown
111: # Git Commit Workflows
112: 
113: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: \## 1. OVERVIEW
118: 
119: ### Purpose
120: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
121: 
122: ### When to Use
123: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
124: - Filtering generated files from commits
125: - Writing clear commit messages
126: 
127: ### Core Principle
128: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
129: ```
130: 
131: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
132: 
133: ```markdown
134: # Git Commit Workflows
135: 
136: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
137: 
138: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
139: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
140: 
141: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
142: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: \## 1. OVERVIEW
147: 
148: ### Purpose
149: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
150: 
151: ### Core Principle
152: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
153: ```
154: 
155: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
156: 
157: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
158: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
159: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
160: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
161: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
162: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
163: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
164: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
165: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ### Reference Body Skeleton
170: 
171: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
172: 
173: ```markdown
174: # [Title]
175: 
176: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 1. OVERVIEW
181: 
182: ### Purpose
183: 
184: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
185: 
186: ### When to Use
187: 
188: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
189: - [Second trigger]
190: 
191: ### Core Principle
192: 
193: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
194: 
195: ### Boundaries
196: 
197: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
198: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
199: 
200: ### Key Sources
201: 
202: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
203: 
204: ---
205: 
206: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
207: 
208: ### [Rule Group]
209: 
210: - **Rule:** [What to do]
211: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
212: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
217: 
218: [Body of the section]
219: 
220: ---
221: 
222: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
223: 
224: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
225: ```
226: 
227: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
228: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
229: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
230: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
231: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
232: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
233: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
234: 
235: ---
236: 
237: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
238: 
239: ### Create Reference File When
240: 
241: **Workflow Complexity**:
242: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
243: - Decision trees with multiple branches
244: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
245: - Systematic debugging procedures
246: 
247: **Technical Depth**:
248: - Root cause analysis required
249: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
250: - Before/after code transformations
251: - Common error patterns and fixes
252: 
253: **Size Threshold**:
254: - Content exceeds 200 lines
255: - Multiple related workflows
256: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
257: 
258: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
259: 
260: **Core Content**:
261: - Overview and "When to Use"
262: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
263: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
264:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
265: - Quick reference
266: 
267: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
268: 
269: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
270: 
271: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
272: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
273: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
274: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
275: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
276: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
277: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
278: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
279: 
280: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
281: 
282: ---
283: 
284: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
285: 
286: ### Core Principle Statements
287: 
288: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
289: 
290: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
291: 
292: **Format**:
293: ```markdown
294: \## 1. OVERVIEW
295: 
296: ### Purpose
297: 
298: [The outcome this reference produces]
299: 
300: ### When to Use
301: 
302: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
303: 
304: ### Core Principle
305: 
306: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
307: ```
308: 
309: **Examples from Real Skills**:
310: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
311: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
312: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
313: 
314: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
315: 
316: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
317: 
318: **Format**:
319: ```markdown
320: ### The [Number] Phases
321: 
322: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
323: 
324: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
325: 
326: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
327: 
328: **Actions**:
329: 1. [Action 1]
330: 2. [Action 2]
331: 
332: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
333: 
334: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
335: 
336: [Similar structure]
337: ```
338: 
339: **Key Elements**:
340: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
341: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
342: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
343: 
344: ### Before/After Code Examples
345: 
346: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
347: 
348: **Format**:
349: ```markdown
350: ### [Pattern Name]
351: 
352: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
353: \```[language]
354: // Bad code with issues
355: // Showing what NOT to do
356: \```
357: 
358: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
359: \```[language]
360: // Good code with fixes
361: // Showing correct approach
362: \```
363: 
364: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
365: ```
366: 
367: **Key Elements**:
368: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
369: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
370: - Inline comments explaining issues
371: - "Why better" rationale
372: 
373: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
374: 
375: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
376: 
377: **Format**:
378: ```markdown
379: ### Common Patterns
380: 
381: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
382: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
383: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
384: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
385: ```
386: 
387: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
388: 
389: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
390: 
391: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
392: 
393: **Format**:
394: \```markdown
395: ### Decision Logic
396: 
397: \```markdown
398: IF [condition A]:
399:   → [Action/Path A]
400:   → [Expected outcome A]
401: 
402: IF [condition B]:
403:   → [Action/Path B]
404:   → [Expected outcome B]
405: 
406: IF [condition C]:
407:   → [Action/Path C]
408:   → [Expected outcome C]
409: \```
410: \```
411: 
412: **Alternative format** (decision tree):
413: \```markdown
414: \```
415: Analyze situation
416: ├─ Condition A met
417: │  └─ Execute Workflow A
418: │     └─ Expected outcome A
419: ├─ Condition B met
420: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
421: │     └─ Expected outcome B
422: └─ Condition C met
423:    └─ Execute Workflow C
424:       └─ Expected outcome C
425: \```
426: \```
427: 
428: ### Validation Checkpoints
429: 
430: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
431: 
432: **Format**:
433: ```markdown
434: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
435: ```
436: 
437: **Examples**:
438: - `files_analyzed`
439: - `artifacts_filtered`
440: - `strategy_determined`
441: - `root_cause_identified`
442: 
443: **Usage**: Reference in quality checklists and debugging
444: 
445: ### Prerequisites Section
446: 
447: **Purpose**: Link to required standards and context
448: 
449: > **PLACEMENT**: Prerequisites go in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph.
450: 
451: **Format**:
452: ```markdown
453: # [Workflow Name]
454: 
455: [1-2 sentence summary only - no prerequisites here]
456: 
457: ---
458: 
459: \## 1. OVERVIEW
460: 
461: ### Prerequisites
462: Follow [standard name] for all implementations:
463: - **[Standard 1]**: [Brief description]
464: - **[Standard 2]**: [Brief description]
465: - See [standard-file.md](./standard-file.md) for complete requirements
466: ```
467: 
468: **Key Elements**:
469: - Appears in Section 1 OVERVIEW, not intro
470: - Links to other reference files
471: - Lists specific requirements
472: 
473: ### Tool Integration References
474: 
475: **Purpose**: Show MCP tool usage, script execution, asset references
476: 
477: **Format for MCP Tools**:
478: \```markdown
479: **Automated [Task] via MCP:**
480: 
481: Instead of [manual approach], use Chrome DevTools MCP:
482: 
483: \```markdown
484: 1. [Step 1]:
485:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
486:    - parameter1: "value"
487:    - parameter2: value
488: 
489: 2. [Step 2]:
490:    [Use tool: mcp__chrome_devtools__tool_name]
491: \```
492: 
493: **What you'll see:**
494: - [Expected output 1]
495: - [Expected output 2]
496: 
497: **Example output:**
498: \```json
499: {
500:   "field": "value",
501:   "data": "example"
502: }
503: \```
504: \```
505: 
506: **Format for Scripts**:
507: ```markdown
508: **See also:** [script_name.js](../scripts/script_name.js) for production-ready implementation
509: ```
510: 
511: **Format for Assets**:
512: ```markdown
513: **See also:** [template-name.md](../assets/template-name.md) for complete templates
514: ```
515: 
516: ### Common Error Patterns
517: 
518: **Purpose**: Document actual errors with explanations
519: 
520: **Format**:
521: \```markdown
522: **Common [System/Browser] Errors:**
523: 
524: \```javascript
525: // [Actual error message]
526: // → [What it means]
527: // → [How to fix]
528: 
529: // [Another error message]
530: // → [What it means]
531: // → [How to fix]
532: \```
533: \```
534: 
535: **Example**:
536: \```markdown
537: **Common Browser Errors:**
538: 
539: \```javascript
540: // Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'X' of undefined
541: // → Variable is undefined, check initialization
542: // → Verify element exists before accessing properties
543: 
544: // Failed to load resource: net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT
545: // → Ad blocker or browser extension blocking resource
546: // → Check Network tab, test with extensions disabled
547: \```
548: \```
549: 
550: ### Scope Limitations
551: 
552: **Purpose**: Explicitly state what's in/out of scope
553: 
554: **Format**:
555: ```markdown
556: **Note:** [Clarification of what IS supported]
557: 
558: **Out of scope:** [What is NOT supported]
559: ```
560: 
561: **Example**:
562: ```markdown
563: **Note:** All browser testing done via Chrome DevTools MCP.
564: 
565: **Out of scope:** Cross-browser testing in Firefox, Safari (MCP is Chrome-only)
566: ```
567: 
568: ### Browser Testing Checklists
569: 
570: **Purpose**: Specific viewport tests with checkboxes
571: 
572: **Format**:
573: \```markdown
574: **Browser Testing Checklist:**
575: 
576: \```markdown
577: □ Chrome (via Chrome DevTools MCP)
578: □ Mobile viewport (375px) - use DevTools emulation
579: □ Tablet viewport (768px) - use DevTools emulation
580: □ Desktop viewport (1920px)
581: □ Test viewport transitions (320px, 768px, 1920px)
582: \```
583: \```
584: 
585: ---
586: 
587: ### Phased Workflow with Checkpoints Example
588: 
589: **Purpose**: Show complete workflow with validation gates
590: 
591: **Format**:
592: ```yaml
593: implementation_workflow:
594:   phase_1_preparation:
595:     purpose: "Gather context and analyze requirements"
596:     actions:
597:       - "Read user request carefully"
598:       - "Identify affected files and systems"
599:       - "Review relevant documentation"
600:     checkpoint: "requirements_understood"
601:     validation_questions:
602:       - "Can I clearly explain what needs to be done?"
603:       - "Do I know which files will change?"
604:       - "Are there any unclear requirements?"
605: 
606:   phase_2_design:
607:     purpose: "Plan the implementation approach"
608:     depends_on: "phase_1_preparation"
609:     actions:
610:       - "Choose simplest solution that works"
611:       - "Identify potential edge cases"
612:       - "Plan validation strategy"
613:     checkpoint: "design_approved"
614:     validation_questions:
615:       - "Is this the simplest approach?"
616:       - "Have I considered edge cases?"
617:       - "Can I test this effectively?"
618: 
619:   phase_3_implementation:
620:     purpose: "Execute the planned changes"
621:     depends_on: "phase_2_design"
622:     actions:
623:       - "Make code changes following standards"
624:       - "Add necessary tests"
625:       - "Update documentation"
626:     checkpoint: "changes_complete"
627:     validation_questions:
628:       - "Do all tests pass?"
629:       - "Is code documented?"
630:       - "Are standards followed?"
631: 
632:   phase_4_validation:
633:     purpose: "Verify correctness and quality"
634:     depends_on: "phase_3_implementation"
635:     actions:
636:       - "Run full test suite"
637:       - "Check code quality metrics"
638:       - "Review against requirements"
639:     checkpoint: "quality_verified"
640:     validation_questions:
641:       - "Do all tests pass?"
642:       - "Are quality metrics met?"
643:       - "Does this satisfy the original request?"
644: ```
645: 
646: **Example in Markdown Reference**:
647: ```markdown
648: ### Implementation Workflow
649: 
650: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
651: 
652: #### Phase 1: Preparation
653:
